parts.label: (i)
parts.answer: The line $AB$ is $\mathbf r=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-\mathbf k+\lambda(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)$. Equating with $l$ gives incompatible component equations, so the lines do not intersect.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Find a vector equation for $AB$ [M1]. Obtain $\mathbf r=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-\mathbf k+\lambda(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j+2\mathbf k)$, or equivalent [A1]. Equate two pairs of components of general points on $AB$ and $l$ and solve for $\lambda$ or $\mu$ [M1]. Obtain a correct value, e.g. $\lambda=0,\mu=-1$ [A1]. Verify that all three component equations are not satisfied and conclude that the lines do not intersect [A1; $\ne$ is enough, e.g. $2\ne0$, and the conclusion must follow correct values]. The printed guidance lists equivalent pair choices and their incompatible third components. Total 5.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: State or imply that the midpoint has position vector $2\mathbf i+\frac32\mathbf j$ [B1]. Substitute it in $2x-y+2z=d$ and find $d$ [M1; use their direction for $AB$ and their midpoint]. Obtain $4x-2y+4z=5$, or equivalent such as $\mathbf r\cdot(2,-1,2)=5/2$ [A1]. Substitute the components of $l$ in the plane equation and solve for $\mu$ [M1; use their plane]. Obtain $\mu=-1/2$ and $\overrightarrow{OP}=\frac32\mathbf i+\frac12\mathbf j$ [A1; coordinates may replace the position vector]. Total 5.
